summary: Model family has a modest but real effect on predictive performance: test ROC-AUC ranges from 0.894 (KNN) to 0.930 (HistGradientBoosting), a spread of 0.035. The boosted/bagged tree ensembles (RandomForest, HistGradientBoosting) modestly but consistently outperform the linear (LogisticRegression) and instance-based (KNN) models, though all four clear the majority-class baseline (0.761 accuracy) by a wide margin, so the choice of family matters far less than simply using a reasonably-tuned model at all.
primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC range across model families (best - worst, test set)
methodological_choices: 80/20 stratified train/test split (seed=42) plus 5-fold stratified CV on the training set as a robustness check; final numbers reported on the held-out test set. Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country) imputed as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped. Categoricals one-hot encoded, numerics standardized, identically for all four models (harmless for tree models, needed for LogisticRegression/KNN) so the comparison isolates model family rather than preprocessing. Compared 4 model families representing different inductive biases: LogisticRegression (linear), KNN (k=25, instance-based), RandomForest (300 trees, bagging), HistGradientBoosting (boosting) — all near-default hyperparameters, no per-model tuning via grid/random search, since the question is about family choice, not tuning effort. ROC-AUC chosen as primary metric over accuracy because the target is imbalanced (~24% positive); accuracy and F1 reported as secondary metrics. No explicit class-imbalance handling (e.g. class_weight, SMOTE) was applied — all models used their default handling of the ~76/24 class split.
